svg.title: Runtime 1.3 to Runtime 2.0: what actually breaks
svg.desc: Fabric Spark runtime migration from 1.3 to 2.0: 6 simultaneous component version moves, GA production vs Preview pilot stance, 4 breakage classes (Python libraries, JVM JARs, ANSI SQL default, Delta 4.x protocol), and post-migration validation with zero-downtime rollback.
svg.text: Runtime 1.3 to Runtime 2.0: What Actually Breaks
Six simultaneous component moves ➔ 4 critical breakage classes ➔ Pre-flight testing & zero-downtime rollback
STAGE 1: SIX COMPONENT LAYERS MOVE SIMULTANEOUSLY

g.title: Component versions move together — Six component layers move at once between Runtime 1.3 and Runtime 2.0.
g.text: • Not a simple patch bump; every layer is an independent breaking surface

g.title: Production stays on GA — Microsoft's guidance is production on GA, with Runtime 2.0 piloted separately.
g.text: • Microsoft official guidance: Keep production workloads on GA release (Runtime 1.3)
• Runtime 2.0 is Public Preview — pilot only in dedicated test/sandbox workspaces
• Never switch production workspaces directly to preview runtimes

svg.text: STAGE 2: THE FOUR BREAKAGE CLASSES & PRE-FLIGHT CHECKS

g.title: Libraries must be re-published — The Python version jump requires libraries to be re-added and published.
JVM artifacts need recompiling — Scala and Java version changes require custom JARs to be recompiled.
ANSI mode flips on — Spark 4.x enables ANSI mode by default, turning silent NULLs into runtime errors.
g.text: ANSI SQL is ON by default in 4.x
• Forces Native Engine to JVM fallback

g.title: Delta protocol interoperability — Delta 4.x-only features raise the table protocol irreversibly and can break other readers.
Verify native execution afterwards — Native execution must be verified after migrating because ANSI forces fallback.
g.text: • The Silent Fallback Trap: ANSI on 2.0 silently forces native operators back to JVM
• Inspect df.explain() to verify NativeScan and NativeProject are active in the final plan
• Review Spark Advisor alerts for fallback warnings

g.title: Rollback is a config change — Runtime is an Environment-level setting, so rollback is a configuration change.
g.text: 8 · Rollback is a Simple Configuration Change
• Runtime version is bound at Environment level, not hardcoded in notebook logic
• Keep the Runtime 1.3 Environment intact — reverting takes 1 click, 0 rebuild time
• Provides immediate escape hatch if unexpected production regressions occur

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Diagram, August 2026. Sourced from Microsoft Fabric Spark Runtime Release Channels & Migration Runbook.
